assumptions: The consensus algorithm and confidence threshold named.
bio.jane/contract.question: What is the consensus of these one or two reads?

description: Merge one or two Sanger reads into a consensus with the ported SeqTrace caller. With two reads (typically a forward and a reverse of the same amplicon) an IUPAC ambiguity code marks a position the two DISAGREE about; with one read there is nothing to disagree with and a code marks a position where no single base cleared the confidence bar. Returns the consensus, how many positions are ambiguous, and how many the consensus's own trimming stage cut from the ends.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

algorithm.description: Bayesian converts each base's Phred to a posterior and combines the reads position by position; legacy lets the higher-confidence base win each position outright. They are different callers, not settings of one.

document.description: the first read: its name or its project file id.

forward_primer.description: the forward primer to cut, 5→3. Only applies when trim_primers is true.

min_conf.description: the confidence a base must clear to be called rather than written as a code. SeqTrace range 1-61.

primer_match.description: the fraction of a primer that must match for it to be cut. 1 is exact; lower tolerates the mismatches a real read carries at its noisy start. Only applies when trim_primers is true. Advanced.

quality_trim.description: trim the consensus's own ends by quality. Note this is the stage primer trimming lives inside, so primer trimming does nothing without it.

reverse_complement_second.description: reverse-complement the second read before merging. A reverse read of the same amplicon needs this; two forward reads do not.

reverse_primer.description: the reverse primer to cut, 5→3. Only applies when trim_primers is true.

second_document.description: the second read, usually the reverse of the same amplicon. Leave empty for a single-read consensus, which is a different question and is reported as one.

trim_end_gaps.description: also cut the gap runs at each end, where only one read reached. With two reads those stretches are single-read consensus and read as agreement when they are not. Advanced.

trim_min_good.description: how many of those bases must clear `min_conf` for the window to be kept. It cannot exceed `trim_window` and is clamped to it rather than refused. Advanced.

trim_primers.description: cut the primers off the consensus ends. It runs INSIDE the quality-trim stage, so turning it on turns that stage on too.

trim_window.description: how many consensus bases the quality-trim mean is taken over. Wider is more forgiving of a single bad base and slower to stop at a genuinely bad end. Advanced.

name: consensus_from_traces

ambiguousPositions.description: positions written as an IUPAC code. Wire it into a gate — but read `readsUsed` first, because the number means two different things

consensus.description: the consensus, compact (no spacers) — what you would export or align

reading.description: the same sentence the editor shows for this run, generated from it

readsUsed.description: how many reads went in. With 1, an ambiguity is low confidence; with 2, it is disagreement

trimmedFromEnds.description: positions the consensus's own trimming stage removed
